source.publisher: National Crime Agency (NECC / JMLIT+ Financial Sanctions Circumvention Cell)
source.title: Red Alert: Exporting High Risk Goods

summary: UK NCA/OFSI/FCDO Red Alert (December 2023, ref. 0737-NECC) warning the financial sector about techniques used to evade sanctions on exports of high-risk goods to Russia for its war in Ukraine. It describes Russia deploying complex supply chains, alternative supply routes and third-country intermediaries (Turkey, UAE, Belarus, China, Serbia, Uzbekistan) to obtain Common High Priority List items such as integrated circuits and dual-use goods, names UK-sanctioned companies involved in procurement and supply, and sets out 14 red flags covering payment patterns, shell-like counterparties, trade-finance documentation and shipping routes indicative of sanctions circumvention.

typologies.label: Trade Based Sanctions Evasion

citations.quote: A customer that significantly overpays for a Common High Priority list item, compared to known market prices.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Red flag 4, page 4 (indicator list). SAN006 doctrine: 'Trade-Based Sanctions Evasion moves value or prohibited goods across a sanctioned boundary by manipulating the trade transaction itself — mispricing an invoice... Large price deviation from benchmark (over/under-pricing)'. Red flag 4 describes exactly this mechanism: a customer significantly overpaying market price for Common High Priority list items, i.e. price manipulation of the invoice itself to move value/goods, not a goods-classification or corporate-structure issue already claimed under dual-use goods/front companies/transshipment. SAN006 is preferred over its twin TBML010 because this NCA/OFSI Red Alert is explicitly framed as sanctions/export-control circumvention.

typologies.label: Name Screening Evasion

citations.quote: The customer’s name or its address is similar to one of the parties on the OFSI consolidated list.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Red flag 9, page 4 (indicator list). SAN005 doctrine: 'Name Screening Evasion is the defeat of list-based screening through the form of the name: aliases, transliterations, suffix variants, deliberate misspellings and word re-orderings that let a listed party transact under a name an exact-match filter never flags.' Red flag 9 describes precisely this vector — a customer name or address that is 'similar to' (not identical to) an OFSI-listed party, i.e. a near-match engineered or coincidental enough to slip past exact-match sanctions screening. This is a screening-evasion technique distinct from the already-claimed front company, transshipment and dual-use goods typologies.

typologies.label: High Risk Jurisdictions

citations.quote: Transactions related to payments for goods on the Common High Priority list, from a company incorporated after 24 February 2022 and based in known diversionary destinations.
Transactions that use open accounts/open lines of credit when the payment services are conducted in conjunction with known diversionary destinations.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Red flags 1 and 12, page 4 (indicator list). SAN008 doctrine: 'High-Risk-Jurisdiction exposure measures how much of an entity's footprint — where it is registered and operates, the corridors it trades, who owns it, who it deals with — touches sanctioned, embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions... the jurisdiction is not an aggravating detail behind another finding; it is the finding.' Red flags 1 and 12 flag a counterparty's own registration/operating location and financing arrangements being tied to 'known diversionary destinations' as the risk signal in itself — a jurisdictional-footprint finding distinct from SAN003 Transshipment (physical routing through an intermediate point) and SAN004 Front Companies (corporate substance), which were already claimed.

extraction_notes: The overpayment red flag (p.4, item 4) did not cleanly match any Knowledge Centre typology (best search score 0.44, and that candidate, TBML002U Under Invoicing, is the opposite direction of value distortion); it is retained only as an indicator, not proposed as a typology link. SAN004 Front Companies is set to medium confidence: the document never uses the term "front company"; the link is inferred from red flags 1 and 6 (recent incorporation, no/low web presence) rather than an explicit statement. Named sanctioned entities (TURKIK UNION, AZU INTERNATIONAL, AEROMOTUS, FLY BRIDGE, NPP ISTOK, ECITECH) reflect UK designations as reported in this document (actions of 8 Aug 2023 and 8 Nov 2023); current designation status was not independently verified. The jurisdictions list mixes the target jurisdiction (RU), named diversion/transshipment jurisdictions (TR, AE, BY, CN, RS, UZ) and the reporting/exposed jurisdiction (GB) without further distinction, since the schema does not separate these roles. Document text was supplied as pre-extracted PDF text with some artefacts of line-wrap (e.g. mid-word spacing); citation quotes were chosen to avoid those artefacts and should be re-verified against the source PDF by the human reviewer. Merged 3 reviewer addition(s) under schema 1.4.0; each carries its review_justification. Extraction-only record retained at data/records/.
